humanities_role_explanation: Artwork images and Wikipedia descriptions supply the items, but the questions test generic visual-understanding dimensions (identity, attribute, location, counting, spatial relation, interaction, reasoning) adapted from SEED-Bench rather than art-historical disciplinary competence such as attribution or iconological analysis.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal VQA: each item pairs an artwork image with a natural-language multiple-choice question and four options.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Seven dimensions: Instance Identity, Instance Attribute, Instance Location, Instance Counting (counting maps to logical_and_quantitative_reasoning), Spatial Relation, Instance Interaction, and Visual-Inspired Reasoning (common-sense or causal reasoning such as inferring intent, cause or future outcomes). The paper also claims questions probe symbolic meaning and narratives, hence interpretation.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to VQA on art and cultural heritage images.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 14 MLLMs: Gemini 2.5, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Aria, Aya Vision, Kimi-VL, Phi-4, Pixtral 12B, InstructBLIP-Vicuna, LLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT, Gemma 3 (4B, 12B, 27B).

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy on multiple-choice questions, per dimension and overall.

summary: The paper introduces VQArt-Bench, a 14,463-question multiple-choice VQA benchmark for art, generated by a multi-agent LLM pipeline (topic selector, question generator, refiner, judge) from Wikipedia artwork descriptions. It evaluates 14 MLLMs across seven visual-understanding dimensions and finds limited performance and a weakness in counting.
key_findings: Gemini 2.5 is best overall (0.71 accuracy); Kimi-VL is the best open-source model (0.67) and beats GPT-4o (0.64). Most models fall below 50% overall; InstructBLIP-Vicuna scores 0.24, below random. Counting is hardest and Visual-Inspired Reasoning easiest. Gemma 3 27B improves on the 4B version by 9 points.
facets_explanation: Questions, correct answers and distractors were produced by an LLM agent pipeline (Topic Selector, Question Generator, Question Refiner, Judge) from Wikipedia descriptions cleaned by an LLM. Experts manually checked a 25% random sample for hallucination. The questions are meant to be answerable from the image, and each has one correct option scored by exact match.
results_explanation: Table 2 reports Gemini 2.5 with Overall Acc. 0.71, converted here to 71 points; this is the headline best score. Random guessing is about 25% with four choices. No human baseline or format comparison is reported.

humanities_role.quote: we use a well-established hierarchy of seven distinct reasoning dimensions derived from [27].

dataset_size.quote: The complete VQArt-Bench benchmark consists of 14,463 high-quality, multiple-choice questions

evaluation_set_size.quote: accuracy refers to the proportion of correctly answered multiple-choice questions relative to the total number of questions.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: without being subject to fine-tuning of any kind

gold_source.quote: Question Generator then crafts nuanced, open-ended questions based on these candidates.
Question Refiner converts these into a challenging multiple-choice format with plausible distractors

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: avoiding questions that would be answerable only by looking to the metadata.

answer_multiplicity.quote: unambiguously answerable from the image, is non-trivial, follows the provided evaluation dimensions and is linguistically sound
